subject: MSA / Order Form — seat selection, provisional remedies, and arbitration scope
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Connors <s.connors@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: MSA / Order Form — seat selection, provisional remedies, and arbitration scope

Sarah — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Before we pull new redlines together for the MSA + Order Form, I want to align on a couple of narrow items where Aurora and Redwood seemed to have different preferences: governing law, venue (court seat), and the carve for provisional/emergency relief.

Quick summary of what we discussed and our suggested compromise options so legal can review:
- Governing law: Redwood prefers Delaware (familiar precedent for SaaS agreements); Aurora prefers Massachusetts (HQ).
- Venue/seat: Aurora asked for Massachusetts courts; Redwood prefers Northern California or Delaware courts if we keep Delaware law.
- Emergency/provisional relief: Aurora wants ability to seek TROs and preliminary injunctions in MA courts without first going to arbitration. Redwood is open to an emergency relief carve, but we want it narrowly drafted ("provisional remedies" limited to injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm, limited discovery, promptly followed by arbitration/merits forum).
- Arbitration: Redwood is willing to arbitrate monetary claims (if any), but we prefer a single professional forum (JAMS or AAA) with seat in CA or NY; Aurora expressed reluctance to bind all disputes to arbitration for injunctive matters.

Attached: initial markup of the MSA (MSA_redline_aurora_20261123.docx) with two alternative proposals — one where governing law/venue are both Delaware; another split approach (Delaware law, MA venue for certain injunctions).

Can you confirm Aurora's non-negotiables so we can draft a final proposal for Tom/legal? Happy to jump on a short follow-up if that helps.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redline_aurora_20261123.docx (tracked changes), OrderForm_20261123_markup.pdf (high-level redlines)

From: Sarah Connors <s.connors@aurorahealth.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — seat selection, provisional remedies, and arbitration scope

Mina — thanks for the write-up and the attachments. Quick answers from Aurora's side:
- Governing law: our legal team strongly prefers Massachusetts law for customer-facing contracts. It's not a hard blocker yet, but it's the default.
- Venue: we prefer state or federal courts located in Suffolk County (Boston), primarily for ease of enforcement against local execs and to align with procurement policy.
- Emergency relief: absolutely need an express carve allowing Aurora to seek temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions in MA courts where appropriate (data protection, HIPAA-adjacent concerns). We would propose language that allows either party to seek provisional remedies in a court of competent jurisdiction before arbitration, and that such proceeds do not waive arbitration for the underlying monetary claims.
- Arbitration: we're open to arbitration for monetary claims but want it to be limited and optional for certain categories (e.g., smaller disputes below a $250k threshold), and we prefer a neutral geographic location (Boston or NY).

I'll circulate this to our GC team and send any specific redline on the MSA by close of business. If Redwood can accept a narrow emergency relief carve that explicitly preserves the right to seek injunctive relief in MA courts, that will get us a lot of traction on our side.

Best,
Sarah Connors
Sr. Director, Vendor Contracts

Marcus / Laura — forwarding Aurora's reply. They are pushing MA law/venue and want an explicit TRO/preliminary injunction carve. I flagged that Redwood can accept a narrow provisional remedies carve but want the drafting to: (1) limit forum-shopping risk; (2) ensure injunctive relief is "preservative" (i.e., temporary) and followed by arbitration/merits in the agreed forum; and (3) keep the governing law in Delaware if at all possible.

Questions for legal ops / GC:
- Is a split approach workable: Governing law = Delaware; Emergency relief = courts in Suffolk County, MA (for Aurora) OR courts of Santa Clara County, CA (for Redwood) depending on the party seeking relief? We could craft reciprocal language that ties the emergency forum to the plaintiff's residence/where harm occurs.
- If we must concede MA law, what are the practical differences we should highlight for sales (indemnity scope, limitation of liability carve-outs, injunctive standards)?

I've attached the latest redlines. I'll draft two short proposal texts for Marcus to review and then send to Sarah.

— Mina

Mina — thanks for the summary. My preferred approach is pragmatic and aims to minimize escalation risk while protecting Redwood's ability to enforce IP/data protections quickly. Suggested elements:

1) Governing law: Delaware. If Aurora insists on MA, ask them to accept Delaware for interpretation of the agreement but concede local law only for statutory claims (very narrow). This gives consistency for contract interpretation.

2) Venue / Forum selection: propose split clause:
   - "Governing Law: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
   - Venue for enforcement of monetary damages: exclusive jurisdiction and venue shall be the state and federal courts located in the County of Santa Clara, California.
   - Provisional remedies/emergency relief: Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional remedies (including temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions) in any court of competent jurisdiction, provided that such relief is limited to preservation of the status quo and does not determine the merits of the dispute. Any party obtaining provisional relief shall promptly submit the underlying dispute to arbitration per Section X.
"

3) Arbitration carve: monetary claims > $250k to arbitration (JAMS Los Angeles or AAA New York as fallback). Small claims / escrow / injunctive matters remain in court.

4) Draft a short "procedural sanity" clause to prevent duplicative proceedings, e.g., an automatic stay provision for parallel actions and streamlined transfer back to the arbitral forum.

I'll draft two redline paragraphs: one that keeps Delaware + Santa Clara + emergency carve above, and a concession version that flips governing law to MA but retains our suggested venue for monetary claims and emergency carve. Once you sign off, send to Sarah with Marcus' suggested language inline.

—Marcus

Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: split-governing-law + provisional remedies carve (redlines attached)

Sarah / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are two clean options in the redline (OrderForm_20261123_markup.pdf and MSA_redline_aurora_20261123.docx):

Option A (Redwood preferred):
- Governing law: Delaware.
- Venue for monetary claims: state and federal courts in Santa Clara County, CA.
- Provisional remedies: Either party may seek provisional remedies (temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction) in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or protect confidential information; such relief shall be provisional only and the underlying dispute shall be submitted to arbitration or otherwise litigated in the forum required for monetary claims.
- Arbitration: monetary claims >= $250,000 to JAMS (Los Angeles) with limited discovery (expedited rules).

Option B (Concession):
- Governing law: Massachusetts.
- Venue for monetary claims: exclusive jurisdiction and venue for monetary damages: state and federal courts in Suffolk County, MA OR arbitration by AAA in NY for claims >= $250k.
- Provisional remedies: same narrow carve as Option A (expressly permitted in MA courts as needed to protect PHI/HIPAA-related risk).

Request: please confirm which option Aurora prefers (A or B) and whether the emergency relief carve as drafted is acceptable. If you want, we can convert Option A into a short two-paragraph "safety valve" clause tying the emergency forum to where the threatened harm is occurring (which would allow either party to go to local courts for immediate relief).

If you accept one of the options, we'll prepare a DocuSign update for the Order Form and the final MSA markup. Link to draft DocuSign packet (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/aurora-orderform-9583

Thanks — appreciate the help moving this over the finish line.

Best,
